newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker wants removal of Comptroller Ludwig.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker wants removal of Comptroller Ludwig.

text.p: A top Democratic lawmaker on Tuesday called for the removal of the U.S. comptroller of the currency, Eugene Ludwig.
Rep. John Dingell, ranking minority member of the House Commerce Committee, said the comptroller was wrong to consider overturning a controversial Rhode Island insurance regulation.

Noting that Ludwig recently recused himself from a decision involving NationsBank Corp, Dingell said in a speech to a Washington meeting of the Independent Insurance Agents of America: "I have to wonder why the reasons for his recusal elsewhere do not apply more broadly."

"In my opinion, recusal is a good first step toward a more productive goal -- removal," Dingell said. "I'm not saying that because I think there are any ethical problems here. This is simply a matter of stupid policy."
The comptroller is considering overturning a Rhode Island insurance regulation that some banks argue gives an unfair preference to insurance agents.

Last year, the Supreme Court ruled that states cannot "significantly interfere" with national banks seeking to sell insurance, giving the comptroller authority to preempt state regulations affecting banks.

But a top Republican lawmaker, House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach of Iowa, said later he did see any reason for the comptroller to be removed. Leach has previously opposed the comptroller's move to reject Rhode Island's rule.
"I'm not advocating the comptroller of the currency step down," Leach told reporters after speaking to the agents.

"There's been no one that's disagreed with the comptroller on a series of issues and powers more than I have," Leach said. "But I think we ought to keep this an issue of substantive differentiation rather than personal job security."
Ludwig last week said he would recuse himself from the decision on two applications from NationsBank for permission to establish real estate-related subsidiaries.

Nationsbank's chief executive had attended a controversial coffee sponsored by the Democratic National Committee at the White House last May that Ludwig also attended. Ludwig has said he would not have attended if he had known of the Democratic National Committee's involvement.
In recusing himself from the NationsBank applications, Ludwig said he wanted to ensure "there can be no question about the integrity of the decision process."
At the time, a spokeswoman for Ludwig said the comptroller was not planning to recuse himself from other matters involving NationsBank or the banks of other executives who attended the coffee.

A spokesman for the Comptroller noted that no decision has been made yet about preempting the Rhode Island law. "We are taking all comments, we'll consider them, including any from a member of Congress," the spokesman said Tuesday.
Dingell also blasted the Comptroller and Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan for advocating excessive bank deregulation in the debate over modernizing U.S. banking laws.

"It appears now that the Comptroller of the Currency and the Chairman of the Fed are competing against one another to see who can strip as many requirements off the banks they regulate," Dingell said. "It is a classic race to the bottom."
If the Comptroller's office nullifies the Rhode Island rule, Banking Committee chairman Leach predicted that Congress would probably not pass a law overturning the Comptroller's decision.
"I doubt if you'd have a Rhode Island specific reaction," he said. "You're probably only likey to have it dealt with only in the context of broad, umbrella types of circumstances."
